clue.text: There's nothing in Shakespeare that's wooden

indicators.note: the word in says the nought sits inside the poet's title

parts.note: Shakespeare is known as the Bard
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A remark that Shakespeare's writing contains nothing but stilted, wooden lines.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: a plank is something wooden, and the clue uses 'wooden' to point at it.
explanation.definitionFit: A plank of timber is a wooden thing, so 'wooden' stands for the flat piece of sawn wood.

clue.text: Flower only three times taking a prize

parts.note: but means only, as in 'but a child'
ter is Latin for three times, used in prescriptions
a cup is a trophy awarded as a prize

explanation.surface: A flower that won a trophy on just three occasions.
explanation.walkthrough: TER is Latin for 'three times', familiar from old prescriptions; 'taking' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A yellow meadow bloom of the genus Ranunculus is a common wild flower.

clue.text: A small section showing some expertise

parts.note: dept is the short form of department, a section

explanation.surface: A minor part of a team that demonstrates a bit of skill.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone skilled and proficient shows expertise in a task.

clue.text: Last month, bands and flags appeared

parts.note: December, abbreviated DEC, is the last month of the year
lines are stripes or bands

explanation.surface: In December, striped bunting and banners went up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flags' looks like banners but is the verb: to grow weaker; 'appeared' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To flag is to tire or weaken, and something that deteriorates or ebbs away does just that.

clue.text: "The Player" by 23 ac

parts.note: per is Latin for by, as in 'per hour'
the answer to 23 across, meaning no longer or prior

explanation.surface: A theatrical credit: a work called The Player, attributed to whoever wrote 23 across.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor or musician who plays a part or piece is an entertainer on stage.

clue.text: Sue, though the compensation appears about right

indicators.note: about means the payment word goes around the letter for right

parts.note: pay is compensation for work

explanation.surface: Someone takes legal action, though the damages look fair enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sue' looks like going to court; here it is the older sense, to plead or beg.
explanation.definitionFit: To sue for something is to petition or beg for it, as in suing for peace, which is to entreat.

clue.text: Keeping people split about pollution

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: split says the word for contamination is broken open to take the people inside

parts.note: a taint is a trace of contamination
men are people

explanation.surface: People divided over a question of environmental contamination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'split' looks like a verb about the people disagreeing; here it says the pollution word is broken open around them, and 'about' gives its own two letters at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Retention, holding on to something, is the act of keeping it.

clue.text: In October one may possibly see "The Fairy King"

indicators.note: In says the name is found inside the run of the two words October one

explanation.surface: An autumn sighting of a fairy king from folklore.
explanation.walkthrough: The king of the fairies in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: In A Midsummer Night's Dream the ruler of the fairies, husband of Titania, is called by this name.

clue.text: The country a comedian made sport of

indicators.note: making sport of the words treats them as playthings, rearranging their letters

explanation.surface: A nation that a comic poked fun at.
explanation.definitionFit: A Balkan nation, now North Macedonia, is a country.

clue.text: Means of measuring a sovereign

explanation.surface: Asking how a monarch is to be measured.
explanation.definitionFit: A straight edge marked in inches measures length, and a monarch is one who governs a realm.

clue.text: Ditch a worker for being sarcastic

parts.note: a ditch is a long dug channel, a trench
the worker ant is the standard crossword worker

explanation.surface: Someone is told to sack a labourer for making snide remarks.
explanation.definitionFit: Biting, cutting criticism is incisive and sharp, which is how sarcastic speech lands.

clue.text: "Let such teach others who themselves —" (Pope)

parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation: the missing word completes a line from Alexander Pope's Essay on Criticism about who should be allowed to teach

explanation.surface: A line of Pope's verse with its last word left blank for the solver.
explanation.walkthrough: The line is from Pope's Essay on Criticism: only those who are outstanding at something should teach it.
explanation.definitionFit: Pope says only those who outshine others in a skill should teach it, so the missing verb means to be outstanding.

clue.text: Bring on late in error

indicators.note: something done in error is done wrongly, so the letters of the two words are mixed up

explanation.surface: A complaint about someone arriving late and being sent on by mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in error' rearranges LATE IN; the first 'in' is fodder, the second is part of the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: To necessitate something as a consequence is to bring it on, the way a plan may involve costs.

clue.text: Complaint of the underworld class

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and his realm
an order is a class or rank, as in a religious or biological order

explanation.surface: A grievance raised by the criminal fraternity.
explanation.definitionFit: An illness or ailment is a medical complaint, such as a stomach upset.

clue.text: Surprised to find a cast off is not ragged inside

indicators.note: inside says the jumbled letters go within the word for discarded

parts.note: to shed is to cast off, as a snake does its skin

indicators.note: ragged means torn and irregular, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Amazed to discover a discarded garment is not frayed on the inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ragged' rearranges the letters of 'is not' into TONIS; 'inside' places them within the word for discarded, after the opening A.
explanation.definitionFit: Amazed or stunned by something unexpected is to be very surprised.

clue.text: Copper and medico being presented to Her Majesty, certain to be awkward

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen
certain, as in 'certain people', means some

explanation.surface: A policeman and a doctor, introduced at court to the Queen, are bound to feel ill at ease.
explanation.walkthrough: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen; 'being presented to' just joins the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bulky and unwieldy is clumsy to handle, which is what awkward means here.

clue.text: Drawing that comes naturally

parts.note: drawing here is not sketching but pulling: the natural attraction of iron towards a lodestone, or of people to a charismatic person

explanation.surface: Praise for an artist whose sketches seem effortless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawing' suggests art; it means pulling, the attractive force of a natural lodestone.
explanation.definitionFit: The natural force by which iron is attracted, or personal charm that pulls people in, is a drawing power.

clue.text: A woman returning to have a meal

indicators.note: returning means the word for eating is written back to front

parts.note: to have a meal is to dine

explanation.surface: A woman coming back home to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Enid is a woman's given name, as in the writer Enid Blyton.

clue.text: Put -off a fellow -.could be -cleaner!

parts.note: to deter is to put off or discourage
a gent is a gentleman, a fellow

explanation.surface: Discourage a chap, and he might end up cleaner.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray dashes are scanning marks in the held clue; the page reads 'Put off a fellow – could be cleaner!'.
explanation.definitionFit: A washing powder or liquid is a cleaning agent, a cleaner.

clue.text: A tool one wants badly

indicators.note: badly means the letters of the two words are put together wrongly

explanation.surface: A tool that someone wants very much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' looks like 'very much' with wants; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine-toothed saw for cutting the projecting joints of woodwork is a carpenter's tool.

clue.text: The young attendant's quiet period

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical mark for quiet
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A young servant enjoying a quiet spell.
explanation.definitionFit: A boy servant at court or a wedding is a young attendant on a knight or bride.

clue.text: Check legislation affecting shops?

explanation.surface: Asking whether a law on retail trade amounts to a restraint.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is whimsical: a law about the counters in shops would be a 'counter act'; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: To check something is to neutralise its effect, and a law on the counters of shops is jokingly a 'counter act'.

clue.text: Blow up article to get lead

parts.note: a gale is a strong wind, a blow

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is written from bottom to top, reversed

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Explode an item to obtain lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blow up' reads as explode, but splits into a strong wind and 'up', which in a down clue turns the article to read NA.
explanation.definitionFit: The principal ore of the metal, lead sulphide, is mined as the source of lead.

clue.text: The plant, when working, emits, call endlessly

indicators.note: working means operating in a new way, so the letters are rearranged
endlessly means the word call loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A garden plant that, when in action, gives off a constant cry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts CALL to CAL, and 'when working' rearranges CAL with EMITS.
explanation.definitionFit: A climbing garden shrub with large flowers is a plant, often grown over walls.

clue.text: Sound Chinese man' who'll believe the worst

indicators.note: sound means the word for Chinese is spoken, giving another word that is pronounced alike

parts.note: Sinic is an adjective meaning Chinese

explanation.surface: A level-headed Chinese man who always expects the worst of people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like an adjective (sensible) but is the homophone signal; the apostrophe after 'man' is a scanning mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who distrusts others' motives and expects the worst of human nature is a sceptic of goodness.

clue.text: No longer prior

explanation.surface: A two-word note that something earlier has ceased to be.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses mean earlier: a one-time holder of an office is no longer in post, and the previous of two is the earlier.

clue.text: Low quarters for a beast

parts.note: to low is to moo like a cow
S and E are two compass points, or quarters

explanation.surface: Humble lodgings meant for an animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low quarters' reads as poor lodgings; low is the cow's call, quarters are compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: A large deer of northern forests, the elk, is a wild animal.

clue.text: Wood surrounding a place of entertainment

indicators.note: surrounding means the tree's name goes around the single letter

parts.note: fir is a softwood timber

explanation.surface: Timber encircling a venue for amusements.
explanation.definitionFit: A funfair with rides and stalls is a venue for amusement and fun.

clue.text: One absorbed in back-issue, bearing the din

indicators.note: absorbed in says the single letter is taken into the middle of the turned word
back means the word for offspring is written backwards

parts.note: issue means offspring, a son
one is the Roman numeral I
a compass bearing such as east gives E

explanation.surface: Someone engrossed in an old magazine copy, putting up with the racket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns SON into NOS; 'absorbed in' puts I inside to make NOIS.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud racket or clamour is a din, unwanted sound.

clue.text: Lead weight — it has grave associations

parts.note: the head is the one at the front, the lead
a stone is a British unit of weight, fourteen pounds

explanation.surface: A heavy lump of lead, said to be linked with burial.
explanation.walkthrough: A stone is a British weight of 14 pounds; 'grave' looks like serious but means a burial place.
explanation.definitionFit: A carved slab set at the top of a burial plot marks a grave, hence the associations.

clue.text: He'll get firm with many an individual, the German boss

parts.note: Co is short for company, a firm
M, the Roman numeral for a thousand, stands for many
a man is an individual person
der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: A boss who will be firm with many a person, the German manager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firm' looks like an adjective (strict) but gives CO, company; 'an' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An officer in charge of a force or unit is the boss, the person giving orders.

clue.text: Centre-forward others twist

indicators.note: centre of the word forward picks its middle letter

parts.note: the rest means the others

explanation.surface: A football striker whose team-mates distort the play.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a centre-forward; split it to take the centre of 'forward', its fourth letter, W.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrench or pull with a twisting movement is to twist something away.
